questions.question: During a complex extraction, a root is displaced into the maxillary sinus. Sami, confident, wants to attempt recovery. Mina, more cautious, says: 'Wait, let's think before we act.' What is the immediate management?
options: Attempt surgical recovery through the socket if the root is visible, otherwise refer to a specialist
Leave the root in place and prescribe prophylactic antibiotics for 10 days
Perform vigorous antro-nasal irrigation to try to expel the root through the ostium
Close the socket hermetically and monitor with CBCT at 6 months
questions.explanation: Mina is right: a root displaced into the sinus requires evaluation by a specialist to avoid chronic sinusitis. Sami, a little annoyed, admits: 'Okay, you're right for once.'

questions.question: A patient on bisphosphonates (oral, < 3 years) requires an extraction. Sami suggests stopping the treatment 6 months before. Mina corrects him: 'No, the recommendations have changed.' What is the current recommendation?
options: Extract with an atraumatic technique, primary suture and antibiotic coverage
Stop bisphosphonates 6 months before and 3 months after surgery
Formally contraindicate extraction and propose coronal devitalization
Perform extraction with extensive alveolectomy to promote secondary healing
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The risk of osteonecrosis is low for oral intake < 3 years. Atraumatic surgery is preferred.' Sami, a little disappointed, retorts: 'I tell you I follow the recommendations!'

questions.question: During an extraction, the patient presents a dislocation of the temporomandibular joint. Sami panics. Mina, calm, says: 'I've seen this before, here's the maneuver.' What is the recommended maneuver?
options: Nelaton's maneuver (downward then backward pressure on the lower molars)
Application of a compressive chin strap for 48 hours
Infiltration of local anesthetic into the masseter muscle to relieve contracture
Reduction by anterior traction only
questions.explanation: Mina performs Nelaton's maneuver skillfully. Sami, impressed, says: 'You saved me, thank you.' She replies: 'That's why I'm here, to fix your mistakes.'

questions.question: Facing a mandibular wisdom tooth whose apex is close to the inferior dental canal, Sami examines the panoramic radiograph. Mina shows him a radiological sign suggestive of a high risk of nerve injury. This sign is:
options: Interruption of the white cortical line of the inferior dental canal
Marked divergence of the distal roots
The presence of a reduced pericoronal follicle
The vertical position of the tooth on the arch
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Interruption of the cortical line is a major sign of proximity to the neurovascular bundle.' Sami, grateful, carefully notes the information.

questions.question: Sami prepares a flap and asks Mina what principle ensures the best tissue vascularization. Mina, without hesitation, answers:
options: The base of the flap must be wider than its free edge (wide pedicle)
The flap must be systematically elevated beyond the mucogingival line
Perform divergent release incisions towards the bottom of the vestibule
A full-thickness incision is always superior to a split-thickness incision
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A wide base ensures optimal vascularization of the flap.' Sami, admiring, says: 'I'll never forget that.'

questions.question: Sami hesitates between a triangular flap and an envelope flap. Mina explains to him that the main advantage of the triangular flap is:
options: Better visibility and access without increasing tissue tension
A shorter operating time because no release incision is needed
A lower risk of long-term gingival recession on adjacent teeth
A total absence of risk of injury to the mental nerve
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The release incision allows better access without excessively stretching the tissues.' Sami, convinced, opts for the triangular flap.

questions.question: Mina treats a persistent dry socket. Despite dressings, the pain remains intense. She says to Sami: 'We need to reassess the diagnosis.' What is the logical approach?
options: Reassess the diagnosis: suspect a bone sequestrum or foreign body
Multiply medicated dressings every 12 hours
Prescribe a combination of third-generation antibiotics
Perform aggressive alveolar curettage until healthy bleeding
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Unusual persistence should suggest an underlying cause (sequestrum, infection).' Sami, impressed by her rigor, says: 'You really are the best.'

questions.question: During an upper 3rd molar extraction, Sami is about to luxate the tooth. Mina stops him and says: 'Careful, we need to prevent tuberosity fracture.' What is the main preventive measure?
options: Luxate the tooth with caution and assess the mobility of the tuberosity bone
Perform systematic peripheral osteotomy before any luxation
Always extract lower teeth before upper ones
Use a curved elevator applied only in the vestibular area
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Early detection of bone mobility allows stopping the extraction before fracture.' Sami, grateful, thanks her.

questions.question: Sami suspects an OAC after a maxillary molar extraction. Mina suggests a simple test to confirm the diagnosis. This test is:
options: The Valsalva maneuver (exhalation with nostrils blocked)
The Bowman probe test in the socket
The retro-alveolar under Clark angle
The pulp vitality test of adjacent teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The Valsalva maneuver allows visualizing the passage of air/bubbles through the socket.' Sami, a little annoyed at not having thought of it, says: 'You're unbeatable.'

questions.question: Mina must use a local hemostatic agent. She explains to Sami that some are contraindicated in cases of acute alveolar infection. These are:
options: Compressed gelatin sponges in septic environments
Oxidized regenerated cellulose (Surgicel)
Resorbable collagen plugs
Simple compression with sterile gauze
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Gelatin can serve as a bacterial nest if not used correctly in a clean socket.' Sami, taking notes, says: 'I'll remember that.'

questions.question: During the use of surgical burs, Sami forgets irrigation. Mina intervenes immediately and explains that the complication to fear is:
options: Thermal necrosis of the alveolar bone preventing healing
Massive subcutaneous emphysema
Irreversible pulpal injury to adjacent teeth
Vertical root fracture of the neighboring tooth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Heat denatures bone cells (osteocytes).' Sami, a little ashamed, says: 'Thank you, I would have made a mistake.'

questions.question: A patient on vitamin K antagonists (VKA) with therapeutic INR requires an extraction. Sami suggests stopping the treatment. Mina, better informed, tells him:
options: Extraction is possible without stopping treatment, with rigorous local hemostasis measures
It must be systematically stopped 5 days before, with heparin relay essential
It must be substituted with aspirin 100mg for 3 days
It must be systematically postponed to a later date
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Current recommendations favor maintaining VKAs if the INR is within the therapeutic target.' Sami, defeated, says: 'You're an encyclopedia on legs.'

questions.question: Sami is about to extract an impacted mandibular wisdom tooth in a lingual position. Mina warns him of a particularly at-risk anatomical structure. This is:
options: The lingual nerve
The facial artery
The lateral pterygoid muscle
Wharton's duct
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The lingual nerve runs along the lingual face of the mandible at the level of the 3rd molars.' Sami, cautious, redoubles his attention.

questions.question: Mina finishes an extraction and checks the socket. She explains to Sami that no root debris should be left. The main reason is:
options: They can act as a foreign body, delay healing or cause infection
They systematically block future implant placement
They inevitably lead to rapid bone resorption
It is a legal obligation regardless of difficulty
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Their persistence is a potential infectious focus.' Sami, carefully inspecting, says: 'I will always check in the future.'

questions.question: A patient returns 3 to 5 days after an extraction with a dull, pulsatile pain. Sami, without hesitation, says to Mina: 'It's a dry socket.' Mina confirms. The pain is:
options: The classic clinical sign of a dry socket
A normal inflammatory reaction of the periosteum
An infection of the submasseteric space
The formation of a residual cyst
questions.explanation: Mina confirms: 'Dry socket classically manifests after 48-72h.' Sami, happy with his diagnosis, says: 'I'm starting to become good.'

questions.question: Mina performs a vestibular advancement flap (Rehrmann flap). Sami asks her its objective. She answers:
options: To close an oroantral communication
To eliminate a large radicular cyst
To facilitate the placement of a removable prosthesis
To drain a periodontal abscess
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'It is the standard technique for closing an OAC.' Sami, observing the procedure, is impressed by her mastery.

questions.question: Sami sutures a flap and asks Mina which type of suture allows better eversion of the wound edges. She answers:
options: Horizontal or vertical mattress suture
Simple interrupted suture
Simple continuous suture
Cross stitch
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Mattress sutures are superior for maintaining edge eversion.' Sami, applying the technique, is satisfied with the result.

questions.question: Sami, happy with his suture, tightens the threads firmly. Mina stops him and says: 'Careful, don't tighten too much.' The reason is:
options: A risk of ischemic necrosis of the tissues due to excess tension
A risk of creating an inclusion cyst
Delayed deep bone healing
An impossibility of removing the threads later
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Excessive tension compresses vessels and necroses the flap.' Sami, loosening his stitches, says: 'Thank you, I almost ruined everything.'

questions.question: Sami asks Mina what 'curettage' of the socket means. She explains to him that it is:
options: The elimination of inflammatory tissues (granuloma) and bone/dental debris
The section of the gum around the tooth
The application of a powerful antiseptic
The reduction of sharp bone edges with a file
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'It is the complete cleaning of the alveolar site.' Sami, performing the curettage, is meticulous.

questions.question: Mina receives a patient presenting with acute cellulitis. She explains to Sami that extraction should be delayed. The reason is:
options: Acute infection requires prior control to reduce the risk of dissemination
Immunocompromised patients can never be operated on
Arterial hypertension is an absolute contraindication
A simple occlusal caries does not justify extraction
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Acute infection requires prior control to reduce the risk of dissemination.' Sami, taking notes, says: 'I'll remember that.'

questions.question: Sami performs an osteotomy before an extraction. Mina asks him why. Sami answers:
options: To create enough space to insert an elevator and luxate the tooth without fracture
To reduce gingival healing time
To allow the use of larger forceps
To avoid the use of burs
questions.explanation: Sami explains: 'Osteotomy is crucial for the extraction pathway.' Mina, satisfied with his answer, says: 'You're progressing, Sami.'

questions.question: Sami extracts a tooth near a cystic lesion. Mina reminds him of the precaution to take:
options: Complete cystectomy of the lesion to prevent recurrence
Wide suture of the socket
Prescription of calcium
Do nothing because the cyst disappears spontaneously
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Removal of the cyst is essential during extraction.' Sami, performing the cystectomy, is meticulous.

questions.question: Mina performs a closure flap for OAC. Sami asks her what the main cause of failure of this technique is. Mina answers:
options: Excessive tension or persistent infection in the sinus
The use of resorbable suture
The application of sterile gauze
Consumption of soft foods
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Tension is the number one enemy of healing.' Sami, ensuring everything is perfect, says: 'I'll never forget that.'

questions.question: Sami, in training, asks Mina what 'luxation' means during an extraction. Mina explains that it is:
options: The movement of the tooth in its socket to rupture the periodontal ligament fibers
The back-and-forth movement of the tooth until it falls out
The application of a vertical traction force
The rotation of the tooth on its axis
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Luxation ruptures the periodontal attachment.' Sami, finally understanding, says: 'Thank you, it's much clearer now.'

questions.question: Mina asks Sami what the objective of a complete preoperative radiographic assessment is. Sami answers:
options: To visualize the roots, adjacent bone and noble anatomical structures
To assess the patient's motivation
To justify the cost of the procedure
To check the condition of other teeth
questions.explanation: Sami explains: 'Imaging is essential for planning and safety.' Mina, proud of him, says: 'You've finally become a real surgeon.'
